title: Annual Report and Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2026

headings.text: Annual Report and Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2026

key_sentences: This has been a year of steady progress for the Trust and for the 2,140 households who live in our homes.
Our tenants told us that repairs matter more to them than anything else.
Total income rose by 10.4% to £8.66 million, mainly because of higher rental income and a capital grant for the Lindley scheme.
All income and expenditure derives from continuing activities.
The board aims to hold free reserves equal to at least three months of operating expenditure.
The financial statements have been prepared under the historical cost convention, modified to include certain investments at fair value.
The average number of employees during the year was 87, an increase of 14 compared with the previous year.
Their tenancies are on the same terms as those of other tenants and they cannot use their position to their advantage.

list_items.text: Rental income is recognised in the period to which it relates, net of rent losses from empty homes.
Housing properties are stated at cost less depreciation, and depreciation is charged on each major component separately:
kitchens over 20 years and bathrooms over 30 years.
Capital grants are recognised as income when the conditions attached to them have been met.
(a) No board member received remuneration during the year.
(b) Travel expenses of £2,180 were reimbursed to six board members.
(c) The Trust purchased no goods or services from businesses connected with board members.
